standard.title: Dolly Blocks for Use in Steel Body Repairs — General Requirements
standard.sector: Production and General Engineering / Hand Tools
standard.description: This standard covers the general requirements for the dolly blocks which are used while working with sheet metal body repairs [1].
standard.scope: This standard covers the general requirements for the dolly blocks which are used while working with sheet metal body repairs [1].

certification.description: Conformity marking is governed by the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, providing third-party assurance of production quality, inspection, and safety testing.
requirements: Dolly blocks must be hot forged from special quality, fine-grain, hot-rolled carbon steel or alloy steels having good wear and shock-resisting qualities. A recommended suitable example of steel is grade 45C8 of IS 1875 : 1978.
The finished dolly block must be through-hardened to maintain a strict hardness range between 40 HRC and 52 HRC to prevent surface deformation under impact.

Dolly blocks are designed for straightening, bumping, shrinking, and finishing sheet metal panels on motor vehicle bodies and fenders. They must never be struck directly with a body repair hammer or any other striking tool.

Defines and illustrates three primary functional surfaces: the Crown (broad, convex working surface), the Beading Edge (rounded apex used to raise a bead), and the Flanging Edge (approximately right-angle rounded surface used to form a flange).

Establishes nine standard typical styles: General Purpose Crowned (2A), General Purpose Anvil (2B), General Purpose Rail (2C), Bead Dolly Block (2D), Heel Dolly Block (2E), Toe Dolly Block (2F), Wedge Dolly Block (2G), Shrinking Dolly Block (2H), and Angle Dolly Block (2J) [2].

Hardness testing must be performed on a fixtured tool or a suitable mounted/unmounted specimen that has been cut using a wet-abrasive or equivalent method to prevent heat-induced annealing or alteration [2].

To avoid structural fragmentation or physical injury, dolly blocks must not be used to strike hard, hardened, or masonry objects (such as concrete, bricks, chisels, axes, or other steel tools). Safety goggles must be worn by the operator and anyone in the immediate vicinity.

Dolly blocks must never be ground, welded, or re-heat-treated. They must be inspected regularly, and their use discontinued at the first sign of cracking. Any surface mushrooming caused by tool usage must be promptly redressed to its original contour using a whetstone or file.
